text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
VERSLO ZINIOS
- The central bank decided to start bankruptcy proceedings against Tauras Bank. Central bank inspectors concluded that the bank was insolvent.
- A government commission will chose the winner of the tender for consultant in the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom on Wednesday out of seven candidates.

- On June 30, a Vilnius second district judge threw out the decision of the state audit that would have forced Utena Beverages to hand over 4.99 million litas of shares to the state, ending a four-year dispute and clearing the way for the securities commission to register Utena's shares.

- Geonafta begin drilling in the Girkaliu resevoir on June 25. The company hopes to get 700,000 tonnes of oil this year from Girkaliu and says the composition of the oil is similar to the Brent Blend pumped in the North Sea.

- Litimpeks finished the distribution of its 60 million litas share emission to Scandinavian and Western investors. The new share capital will be registered when the central bank confirms the sources of the new investments.

- The privatisation agency announced its July privatisation list, including six objects to be sold by open competition, 21 to be sold by auction at the privatisation agency and 19 by auction at the stock exchange.
LIETUVOS RYTAS
- Two Lithuanians were arrested in a Miami hotel for attempting to sell nuclear weapons and anti-aircraft rockets.

- Members of parliament grilled central bank governor Reinoldijus Sharkinas on the fall of Tauras Bank and the decision during the government of former Prime Minister Adolfas Shlezhevichius to distribute a 17 million ECU loan from the European Union through Tauras.
- Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius sent a letter to German Chancellor Helmut Kohl saying that Lithuania is ready for negotiations with the E.U. over membership.

- The finance ministry hasd not received any applications to participate in the tender to sell Lithuanian State Commercial Bank. The tender was announced on June 4 and only four banks - two from Lithuania and two foreign banks - bought a set of documents for the privatisation.

- The Siauliai Bank, Lithuania's only regional bank, sold its 14 million litas new share issue. Some 6.8 million litas of shares were bought by shareholders and 7.2 million litas by U.S. investment fund the Baltic Fund. The bank's share capital will increase from 20 million litas to 34 million litas
- The board of the central bank allowed Snoras Bank to start a representation in Sofia Bulgaria.
- Three percent of Klaipeda Nafta was sold for 2.7 million litas at 100 litas a share on Tuesday at the bourse.
RESPUBLIKA
- Parliament on Tuesday rejected amendments suggested by President Algirdas Brazauskas and passed for the second time the law on property restitution.

- President Brazauskas continued his reign atop public opinion polls, with positive ratings of 62 percent. Former deputy prosecutor general Arturas Paulauskas ranked second at 57 percent and Lithuanian-American Valdas Adamkus was third with 56 percent. Lithuanian Parliamentary Chairman Vytautas Landsbergis trailed in a distant seventh place.
LIETUVOS AIDAS
- The government changed its position on the financing of the Butinge oil terminal, deciding on June 26 to grant a state gurantee for loans of $101.575 million for its construction.
-- Burton Frierson, Vilnius newsroom +370 2 22 35 17
